title: Line height: tight, comfortable, loose
summary: The same paragraph at line-height 1, 1.5 and 2, and why the number has no unit.
explanation: line-height sets the height of each line box. At 1 the lines nearly touch and long text is tiring to read; around 1.5 is comfortable for body text; 2 starts to fall apart into separate lines. Headings usually want less (1.1 to 1.25) because their letters are big.

Write it without a unit. A unitless 1.5 means 1.5 times the element's own font size, and children recalculate it for their own size. line-height: 24px would be inherited as a fixed 24px, so a big heading inside would have its lines overlap.
tryThis: Change the .loose font-size to 24px: its lines grow with it, because 2 is relative.
Set .tight to line-height: 16px and its font-size to 24px: the lines overlap.
Find the value between 1.4 and 1.7 that reads best to you.

children.text: line-height: 1. Lines sit right on top of each other, so the eye struggles to find the start of the next one when the text runs long.
line-height: 1.5. There is room between lines, so a paragraph reads smoothly. This is a good default for body text.
line-height: 2. Lines drift apart and the paragraph stops looking like one block of thought.
